"**I is odd in K**, so it breaks the K → −K symmetry and makes the breaking of ρ physical (§2)." ([toy note §5](../papers/reciprocity-toy-models.md#5-matter-and-locality); see flag 2 in [`review/wiki-build-flags.md`](../../review/wiki-build-flags.md)). Model I without matter is symmetric under K → −K as well as under ρ, so its vacuum keeps the combination ρ∘(K → −K), which acts on H exactly as ρ does, and calling ρ broken is a labelling choice.
